title: Angle Creation
shortDefinition: Angle creation changes body or hip position so your force attacks weak structure instead of pushing straight into strength.
whyItMatters: Many techniques fail because the grip is correct but the angle is wrong.
deepExplanation: Angles come from hip heist, head position, shoulder-line cuts, knee cuts, back steps, or pivots. Good angle makes the opponent defend one direction while you move another.
beginnerView: If pushing fails, do not push harder; change angle.
advancedView: Create angles from the opponent’s reaction, not only your footwork.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Angle Creation during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Angle Creation to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Angle Creation is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Angle Creation before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
